summary: Reconnect WAL converges redis-AOF style: unsynced event appends, fsync only on reserved/terminal/ack, poison on failed append, online compaction with a 2x floor, ledger counts only unresolved ids, export/delete/GC refuse only a live owner and remove the WAL.
notes: Design adjusted vs original row: events are buffered (appended without fsync) instead of removed; WAL kept after clean close for cross-process idempotency; no .torn copy for WAL (torn append was never acknowledged). Compaction waits for 2x the last compacted size; without it live state near the threshold rewrote per append (562s quadratic test run). 20k ledger check moved to a ReplayState unit test because the sequential harness costs ~81ms CPU per request.
